items.src: Civils Prelims 2016
items.s:
Regarding the taxation system of Krishna Devaraya, the ruler of Vijayanagar, consider the following statements:

A. The tax rate on land was fixed depending on the quality of the land.

B. Private owners of workshops paid an industries tax.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
items.x: Both are correct: Krishnadevaraya's land tax varied with the quality of land, and private owners of workshops paid an industries tax (UPSC 2016 key: both). (Moved: Vijayanagara administration and revenue, book 1 row 121.)

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: By becoming first graduate in Andhra who was the woman that set an ideal example to the entire women of Andhra?
items.x: The APPSC key names Rukmini Lakshmipathi as the first woman graduate of Andhra and a role model for Andhra women.

items.src: AP High Court Assistant Examiner-2 2021
items.s: Who among the following was popularly known as Punjab Kesari?
items.x: Lala Lajpat Rai was popularly known as 'Punjab Kesari'.

items.src: APPSC Group-2 PYQ
items.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
o: Kandukuri Veeresalingam is known as the father of renaissance movement in Andhra
" The Crescent " is an English weekly founded by Mutnuri Krishna Rao
Andhra Patrika is the first Telugu political newsweekly
Krishna Patrika was started in 1902 by Konda Venkatappaya
items.x: The Crescent was Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty's English paper, not Mutnuri's, so that statement is the incorrect one. Statement 3 is also loose – the first Telugu political weekly was Andhra Prakasika – but The Crescent is the clear error.

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: The socialist party and Praja Socialist party merged with which party in 1977?
items.x: In 1977 the Socialist Party (and the old PSP stream) merged into the Janata Party, along with the Congress (O), Jana Sangh and BLD.

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: Who was the leader in Andhra actively associated with Justice Party
o: All the given answers are correct
items.x: Tripuraneni Ramaswamy, C.R. Reddy and Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu were all associated with the Justice Party in Andhra.

items.src: APPSC AP History PYQ
items.s: Who is the author of the book "Hindu Desha Daridryam"?
items.x: Attili Suryanarayana wrote 'Hindu Desa Daridryam' during the Vandemataram period.

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: Which woman earned good name by distributing proscribed literature during Freedom movement?
items.x: The 2017 APPSC key gives Dronamraju Lakshmibayamma as the woman known for distributing banned (proscribed) literature in the freedom movement.

items.src: Indian History previous paper (header not legible)
items.s: Name the Principal of the Anglo-oriental college, Aligarh, that changed the attitude of Sir Sayyad Ahmed Khan towards the Indian National Congress.
items.x: Theodore Beck, Principal of the MAO College (1883-99), turned Sir Syed against the Congress and encouraged Muslim separatism; Morison came after him.

items.src: U.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2013 +1 more
items.s: Which of the following session of the Indian National Congress, Gandhi said, 'Gandhi may die, but Gandhism will remain forever"?
items.x: Gandhi's words 'Gandhi may die but Gandhism will live for ever' are linked to the Karachi session of 1931.

items.src: Police Constable Preliminary Exam 2016
items.s: Which one of the following was not actually part of the original plan of the non-co operation movement but acquired great popularity among the movement in many parts of the country.
o: Picketing of shops selling foreign cloths
Boycott of Government schools and colleges
Boycott of public transport and communication system
items.x: Picketing of toddy shops was not in the original NCM programme of 1920 but became widely popular; boycott of schools and foreign cloth were part of the plan, and transport was never boycotted.

items.src: SSC 2014
items.s: The first atom bomb was dropped on Hiroshima on
items.x: The first atom bomb was dropped on Hiroshima on 6 August 1945, and Nagasaki followed on 9 August. Options (a) and (d) are identical, so (a) is keyed.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer in A.P. Tribal Welfar
items.s:
A: The Textile Industry of Andhra which flourished during 17th-18th centuries witnessed a decline in the 19th century in both foreign and local markets.
R: In the foreign markets it declined because of competition with machine made goods while in local markets it declined because of high tariffs.
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
items.x: A is true. R reverses the causes: in foreign (British) markets Indian cloth was shut out by high tariffs, while in local markets it lost to cheap machine-made British goods. So R is false (printed key: both true).

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
items.s: Which one was not a cause of social reform movements in India
items.x: Western education, the press and missionary criticism caused the reform movements; female infanticide was one of the evils they attacked, not a cause (options of the original question are lost).

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
items.s: In which one of the following Districts of Andhra Pradesh, "Butta Bommalu"- famous handicrafts is available?
o: East Godavari and West Godavari districts
items.x: Butta Bommalu (light wooden toys) are made at Tanuku, West Godavari – the Godavari districts.

items.src: M.P. P.C.S. (Pre) 2021
items.s: Who called the Congress Conference as the "Annual National Festival of Educated Indians"?
items.x: Lajpat Rai called the Congress sessions the 'annual national festival of educated Indians'.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
items.s: Whose philosophy is reflected in the current primary education of India?
items.x:
Printed key: Tagore. Most books and keys tie primary (basic) education to Gandhi's Nai Talim (general knowledge, not checked).
Gandhi's Basic Education (Nai Talim, Wardha scheme 1937) of learning through work is the philosophy usually said to underlie India's primary education; Tagore's Santiniketan model is a distractor.

items.src: U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2013
items.s: Who among the following had demanded first the dominion status for India?
o: Pt. Motilal Nehru and Govind Ballabh Pant
Sir Tej Bahadur Sapru and Jaykar
items.x: The printed key (UPPCS 2013) names the Liberal leaders Tej Bahadur Sapru and M.R. Jayakar. The library does not settle "first"; Motilal Nehru's 1926 call is also cited, but Pant was not involved, so the Sapru-Jayakar option is kept.

items.src: Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in A.P BC We
items.s: Which are stated to be last words of Mahatma Gandhi?
items.x: Gandhi's last words when he was shot on 30 January 1948 are recorded as 'He Ram'.

items.src: U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2013
items.s: The book “Springing Tiger” is the biography of :
items.x: Hugh Toye's The Springing Tiger is a biography of Subhas Chandra Bose and the INA.

items.src: Deputy Information Engineers & in Sector of Boilers 2019
items.s: Which document among the following is known as 'Magna Carta of Education' in India?
items.x: Wood's Despatch (1854) is called the 'Magna Carta of English Education in India'; the printed '1954' is a typo for 1854. An education-history question, moved to the Wood's Despatch row.

items.src: WBCS 2008
items.s: Who defended Aurobindo Ghosh in the ‘Alipore Bomb Case’?
items.x: Chittaranjan Das defended Aurobindo in the Alipore Bomb Case; he was acquitted in 1909.

items.src: APPSC Asst. Social Welfare Officer, Asst. Tribal Welfare Off
items.s: "Prataparudriyam", a rhetorical work, which describes the nature of "Prataparudra's" character was composed by
items.x: Vidyanatha's Prataparudriyam (Prataparudra Yasobhushanam) is a Sanskrit work on poetics (alankara) with verses praising Kakatiya Prataparudra. Do not confuse it with the later Telugu play Prataparudriyam of Vedam Venkataraya Sastri.

items.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
items.s: Who presided over The Andhra Mahasabha Conference held at Guntur in January 1951?
items.x: The last session of the Andhra Mahasabha at Guntur (13-14 January 1951) was presided over by Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao.

items.src: APPSC Asst. Social Welfare Officer, Asst. Tribal Welfare Off
items.s: 'Antaranolla Atmakathalu' was written by
items.x: The printed key attributes 'Antaranolla Atmakathalu' (autobiographies of untouchables) to the Dalit poet Endluri Sudhakar; no source in the library or on the web confirmed it.

items.src: State PSC
items.s: ‘Satyamev Jayate’, which is engraved on the Indian Emblem, has been taken from –
items.x: Satyameva Jayate on the State Emblem is taken from the Mundaka Upanishad, not the Rig Veda, the Gita or the Matsya Purana.

items.src: Dy. E.O 2008
items.s: Who said that 'Telugu word for word explanation is very meaningful'?
items.x: C.P. Brown, compiler of the Telugu-English dictionaries and editor of Vemana's verses, is the scholar credited with this praise of Telugu; Clive and Medasani Mohan are unconnected (general knowledge, not checked).

items.src: UPPSC (Mains) 2001
items.s: Who among the following was offered the membership of the Royal Asiatic Society of Paris?
items.x: Rammohan Roy was honoured by the Société Asiatique of Paris; the others are not linked with it.

items.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Fisheries in A.P. Fisheries Serv
items.s: Who got the best actress award in the Nandi Awards for 2013 awarded by Government of Andhra Pradesh?
items.x: Anjali Patil won the Nandi best actress award for 2013 for Na Bangaaru Talli.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
items.s: When did Sikkim became the part of India?
items.x: Sikkim became the 22nd State of India by the 36th Amendment in May 1975.

items.src: Assistant Social/BC/Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-I 20
items.s: Why Calico Act was passed by British Government in 1721?
o: To prescribe sizes for books bound with Calico
To regulate the price of Calico Cloth
To levy import tariffs on Calico Cloth
To ban imports of printed cotton textiles
items.x:
Most books and keys: the 1721 Act banned imports of printed cotton textiles. Strictly: the 1700 Act banned imports of printed calicoes; the 1721 Act went further and banned the sale and wearing of most cotton cloth (general knowledge, not checked).
The British Calico Acts protected English wool and silk makers against Indian printed cottons; the option 'to ban imports of printed cotton textiles' is the keyed purpose.

items.src: Civil Assistant Surgeon, Vaidya Vidhana Parishad 2017
items.s: Who is the founder of Aligarh Movement?
items.x: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan founded the Aligarh Movement (MAO College, 1875). (Off-topic; moved.)

items.src: UPSC CSE Prelims 1999
items.s: The most short-lived of all of Britain's constitutional experiments in India was the:
items.x: The UPSC 1999 key is the Indian Councils Act, 1909: it worked only from 1909/10 until the 1919 Act replaced it (in force 1921). Ramsay MacDonald called it an incomplete deal between democracy and bureaucracy.

items.src: Assistant Director in A.P. Economics and Statistics
items.s: Who stated in 1905 that "Self Government is the only remedy for India's woes and wrongs"
items.x: The line 'Self-government is the only remedy for India's woes and wrongs' is Dadabhai Naoroji's, who made self-government (Swaraj) the Congress goal at Calcutta in 1906. Gokhale, Banerjea and Tilak are not credited with it.

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: Who was the exponent to state that the origin of Telugu is from Sanskrit?
items.x: Chilukuri Narayana Rao (Andhra Bhasha Charitramu) argued that Telugu was born of Sanskrit and the Prakrits; Bishop Caldwell held the opposite, that Telugu is a Dravidian language. (Moved: Telugu language and literature row.)

items.src: APPSC Asst. BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper-II 2017
items.s: What was the opinion expressed on the killing of Alluri Sitarama Raju by British in Andhra Patrika of 8th May 1924?
o: Shivaaji and Rana Pratap of Andhra
items.x: The keyed answer is that Andhra Patrika (8 May 1924) called Alluri a great national hero. The comparisons with Shivaji, Lenin or Washington are distractors. Not found in the library.

items.src: Indian History previous paper (header not legible)
items.s: Leaders of the Singh Sabha Movement established the Khalsa College in Amritsar in the year
items.x: Singh Sabha leaders laid the foundation of the Khalsa College, Amritsar, in 1892.

items.src: AP Grama Ward Sachivalayam Village Horticulture Assistant 20
items.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Rajputs of 8th to 14th Centuries :

A. The term Rajput is derived from "Rajaputra", meaning the son of a ruler.

B. They were a group of warriors who claimed Kshatriya caste status.
The correct statements are
items.x: 'Rajput' comes from 'Rajaputra' (son of a ruler), and the Rajputs were warrior lineages claiming Kshatriya status, so both are true. Moved.

items.src: NDA 2008
items.s: With which one of the following is the Tennis Court Oath associated?
items.x: The Tennis Court Oath (20 June 1789) was sworn by the Third Estate deputies of the National Assembly at Versailles, at the start of the French Revolution.

items.src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
items.x: Andhra Patrika–Kasinathuni (c), Krishna Patrika–Konda Venkatappayya (a), Andhra Prakasika–Parthasarathi Naidu (d), The Crescent–Gazulu Lakshminarasu Chetty (b): 1-c, 2-a, 3-d, 4-b.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-II(A) Engineering Assistant
items.s:
Match the following correctly with respect to Mahasabha and corresponding leaders:

A. Visalandhra Mahasabha - i.
C. Rajagopalachari

B. Rayalaseema Mahasabha - ii. Durgabai Deshmukh
C. Andhra Mahila Sabha - iii. C.L.N. Reddy, K. Subrahmanyam and others

D. Dakshina Pradesh - iv. A. Kaleswara Rao
items.x: Visalandhra Mahasabha – A. Kaleswara Rao (iv); Rayalaseema Mahasabha – C.L.N. Reddy, K. Subrahmanyam (iii); Andhra Mahila Sabha – Durgabai Deshmukh (ii); Dakshina Pradesh – C. Rajagopalachari (i).

items.src: Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
items.s: What did Mahatma Gandhi do on the first independence day, i.e., 15-08-1947?
o: He undertook a 24-hour fast at Kolkata.
He unveiled the tricolour on Red Fort.
He oversaw the procession of lakhs of people at Raisina Hill.
He addressed a massive public meeting on communal harmony at Kolkata.
items.x: On 15 August 1947 Gandhiji was in Calcutta working for communal peace and marked the day with a 24-hour fast (and spinning); he did not hoist the flag at the Red Fort.

items.src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
items.s: Which of the following bank was founded by Lala Lajpat Rai at Lahore in 1894
items.x: Lala Lajpat Rai was among the founders of the Punjab National Bank at Lahore (1894).

items.src: NDA 2019
items.s:
Consider the following statements concerning the American war of Independence.

I. The Americans raised the slogan, “No taxation without representation.”

II. The American merchants resorted to boycott the British products.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
items.x: The colonists raised 'No taxation without representation' and American merchants boycotted British goods. Both are correct.

items.src: CDS 2010
items.s: The first Emperor of France was
items.x: Napoleon Bonaparte became Emperor of the French in 1804, the first emperor of France; Charlemagne was emperor of the Romans (800), and Louis XIV a king.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
items.s: The term '3H' concept of Education was given by
items.x:
Most Indian keys: Mahatma Gandhi (Nai Talim). Strictly: the head-heart-hand idea comes from J.H. Pestalozzi (18th-19th c.), from whom Gandhi took it (general knowledge, not checked).
Indian exam keys credit the '3H' formula (Head, Heart, Hand) to Gandhi's basic education (Nai Talim), which taught the hand along with the head and heart. The formula itself goes back to the Swiss educator Pestalozzi.

items.src: APPSC Technical Assistant in Police Transport Organisation 2
items.s: In which country did the Industrial Revolution start first?
items.x: The Industrial Revolution began in England (Britain) in the late 18th century, then spread to France, Germany and the USA.

items.src: APPSC Endowment (Prelims) General Studies 2022
items.s: Who narrated Bhagavata Puranam to Parikshita Maharaja?
items.x: Sage Shuka (son of Vyasa) narrated the Bhagavata Purana to King Parikshit; Suta later retold it to Shaunaka and the sages. (Off-topic; moved.)

items.src: APPSC Group-II 2011
items.s: In Andhra Pradesh State, the 1973 land reforms Act was introduced according to the suggestions made by
items.x: The 1973 AP Act lowered ceilings and made the family the unit along the national guidelines of 1972 evolved through the Central Land Reforms Committee.

items.src: Civil Services (Preliminary) 1998
items.s:
Who started the educational reform movements among Muslims in India?

A. Sir Syed Ahmed Khan

B. Sir W. W. Hunter

C. Shah Wali Ullah

D. Zakir Hussain
Select the correct answer using the codes given below
items.x: Sir Syed Ahmed Khan (Aligarh) and Zakir Hussain (Jamia Millia, basic education) led educational reform among Muslims; Hunter only wrote 'The Indian Musalmans' and Shah Wali Ullah was an 18th-century theologian. (Off-topic; moved.)

items.src: Astt. Comm. 2019
items.s:
Which of the following statements about the Arya Samaj which emerged in the late 19th century are correct?

I. Had a strong supporting base amongst the trading castes.

II. Introduced ‘Shuddhi’ or mass purification.

III. The moderates in the Arya Samaj were headed by Hans Raj and Lajpat Rai and set up a chain of Dayananda Anglo-Vedic Colleges.

IV. The Arya Samaj had fewer membery than the Brahmo Samaj.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
items.x: The Arya Samaj drew on the trading castes (I), started Shuddhi (II) and its College Party under Hansraj and Lajpat Rai ran the DAV colleges (III); its following was larger than the Brahmo Samaj's, so IV is wrong.

items.src: I.A.S. (Pre) 2007
items.s: Who wrote the book-The Story of The Integration of the Indian States?
items.x: 'The Story of the Integration of the Indian States' was written by V.P. Menon, Secretary of the States Department under Patel.

items.src: IAS (Pre) 2010
items.s:
Consider the following statements.

I. The ‘Bombay Manifesto’ signed in 1936 openly opposed the preaching of socialist ideals.

II. It evoked support from a large section of business community from all across India.
Which of the statements given above is/are are correct?
items.x: In May 1936 twenty-one Bombay businessmen signed the 'Bombay Manifesto' openly attacking Nehru's preaching of socialism (I is right). Most of the business class did not join it, and many criticised it, so II is wrong.

items.src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-II Rural Dev
items.s: In Madras State, the Local Boards Act was passed in which of the following years?
items.x: The Madras Local Boards Act was passed in 1884 (after Ripon's 1882 resolution), creating village unions, taluk boards and district boards.

items.src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
items.s: Which governor general eased the entry of British investors and traders into India without any problems?
items.x: Under Bentinck the Charter Act of 1833 ended the Company's trade and let Europeans settle and buy land freely, easing the entry of British investors and traders.

items.src: UPSC CSE Prelims 1998
items.s:
Which of the following pairs are correctly matched?
I. Theodore Beck — Mohammadan Anglo-Oriental College
II. Ilbert Bill — Ripon
III. Pherozeshah Mehta — Indian National Congress
IV. Badruddin Tyabji — Muslim League
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
items.x: Beck – MAO College, Ilbert Bill – Ripon and Pherozeshah Mehta – INC are right; Badruddin Tyabji was INC President (1887), not a Muslim League man – so I, II and III.

items.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
items.s: Who said that 'The first principle of teaching is that nothing can be taught'?
items.x: 'The first principle of true teaching is that nothing can be taught' is Sri Aurobindo's, from A System of National Education (1910).

items.src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
items.s: Who was the author of our National Anthem?
items.x: Rabindranath Tagore wrote Jana Gana Mana, the National Anthem; Bankim Chandra wrote Vande Mataram, the National Song.

items.src: Police Constable Final Written 2019
items.s: In 1918 'India In Transition' was written by
items.x: 'India in Transition' (1918) was written by the Aga Khan III; M.N. Roy's book of the same name came in 1922.

items.src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
items.s: Which period was marked by the rapid growth of public opinion for Telugu identity and shift from problems of the people to a province for the people, from District Conferences to a separate Andhra Conference?
items.x: Public opinion for a Telugu province grew from the Vandemataram movement (1907) to the first Andhra Conference at Bapatla (1913), when district conferences gave way to an Andhra Conference.

items.src: U.P. U.D.A./L.D.A. (Pre) 2001 +1 more
items.s: Which one of the following leaders of the Congress was totally in favour of Cabinet Mission Plan?
items.x:
Printed key: Mahatma Gandhi. gktoday.in gives Sardar Patel, and Azad (India Wins Freedom) claimed the plan as his own; general knowledge, not checked.
The printed key holds that Gandhi was wholly in favour of the Cabinet Mission Plan, which he called the best document the British could have produced.

items.src: APPSC AP History PYQ
items.s: Who among the following were traditionalists who worked against Veeresalingam Pantulu's reforms?
items.x: Kokkonda Venkataratnam led the orthodox attack on women's education and widow remarriage, and A.P. Parthasarathi Naidu also opposed Veeresalingam; Uma Ranganayakulu was his ally (Veeresalingam wrote in his Purushartha Pradayini), so options with him are wrong.

items.src: Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional Servic
items.s: Out of the below, Who was the first graduate from the Calcutta University in 1858?
items.x: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay (with Jadunath Bose) was among the first graduates of Calcutta University in 1858.

items.src: Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in A.P BC We
items.s: In known history, which is the deadliest military conflict in the world in terms of total casualties?
items.x: The Second World War (1939-45) is the deadliest conflict in recorded history, with about 70-85 million dead. The First World War killed far fewer, and the Kalinga war and the Hundred Years' War are much smaller.

items.src: U.P.P.C.S. (Pre) 2014
items.s: Which one of the following is not correctly matched?
o: Bhagwati Charan Vohra : The Philosophy of Bomb
items.x: 'The Indian Sociologist' was Shyamji Krishna Varma's London journal, not Bhagat Singh's. Sanyal wrote Bandi Jivan, Vohra wrote The Philosophy of the Bomb, and Lala Ram Saran Das wrote Dreamland (introduced by Bhagat Singh).

items.src: Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Officers, As
items.s: Which lady is known as the mother of "Indian Revolution"
items.x: Madam Bhikaji Cama, who unfurled the Indian flag at Stuttgart in 1907, is popularly called the 'Mother of the Indian Revolution'. Annie Besant led the Home Rule League, and Kanaklata Barua was a 1942 martyr.

items.src: Asst. Chemical Examiner 2011
items.s: In whose rule Kalidasa lived?
items.x: Kalidasa is traditionally placed at the court of Chandragupta II Vikramaditya (Gupta age); 'Vikramaditya' alone is the title, not a separate ruler here.

items.src: APPSC Assistant B.C. Welfare Officer, Assistant Social Welfa
items.s: The branch of philosophy that is concerned with reasoning is called
items.x: Logic is the branch of philosophy concerned with the principles of correct reasoning (in Indian thought, the Nyaya school).

items.src: RRB 2005
items.s: Who was the first to circumnavigate the earth?
items.x: Ferdinand Magellan's Spanish expedition (1519-22) made the first circumnavigation of the earth; Magellan was killed in the Philippines and Elcano completed it. Cook and Amundsen came much later.

items.src: AEE 2011
items.s: This leader toured Andhra during the Vande-matharam movement
items.x: Bipin Chandra Pal toured Andhra in April 1907 during the Vande Mataram movement.

items.src: UPPSC (Pre) 2014
items.s: Who of the following had regarded the Karachi Session of the Indian National Congress (1931) as the pinnacle of Mahatma Gandhi’s popularity and prestige?
items.x: Subhas Chandra Bose described the Karachi Congress (1931) as the pinnacle of Gandhi's popularity and prestige.

items.src: Grama Ward Sachivalayam Category-III Village Agriculture Ass
items.s:
Match the following correctly:

A. Durgabai Deshmukh - i. 1862

B. Potti Sriramulu - ii. 1880

C. Pattabhi Sitaramaiah - iii. 1901

D. Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu - iv. 1909
Find the correct answer.
items.x: Raghupati Venkataratnam Naidu 1862, Pattabhi Sitaramayya 1880, Potti Sriramulu 1901, Durgabai Deshmukh 1909: A-iv, B-iii, C-ii, D-i.

items.src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
items.s: Who was the nationalist poet to use the word Tenugutalli for the first time in Telugu nationalist writings?
items.x: Exam keys credit Rayaprolu Subbarao, the Telugu nationalist poet of Janmabhoomi and Andhravali, with first using 'Tenugu talli' in nationalist verse. Viswanatha, Jashuva and Kodali Venkata Ratnam are distractors. Not found in the library or on the web.
